facts.text: Newburyport was officially incorporated in 1764 when the Massachusetts General Court split the original town of Newbury into a new seaport community.
The Merrimack River’s south bank, where Newburyport sits, was first inhabited by the Pawtucket Tribe before European settlement.
The city’s historic waterfront still hosts the oldest operating bank in the United States, the Newburyport Five Cents Savings Bank, founded in 1854.
In 1740, English preacher George Whitefield visited Newburyport, inspiring the First Great Awakening with his powerful sermons.
During the 1950s and 1960s, Newburyport’s downtown fell into disrepair, but a federal grant in 1970 saved most historic buildings from demolition.
Every August, the Newburyport Chamber Music Festival brings international artists to the town, offering free concerts and open rehearsals in historic homes.
